learn: In simple meter (2/4, 3/4, 4/4), each beat divides into two.
In compound meter (6/8, 9/8, 12/8), each beat divides into three.
A jig in 6/8 has two beats, each with three pulses.
check: In simple meter, beats divide into...
lessons.try: Conduct 4/4 and 6/8, feeling the difference.

learn: Irregular meters like 5/4 and 7/8 group beats unevenly (3+2, 2+2+3).
Some pieces change meter often.
Many folk traditions, like Balkan music, use irregular meters.
lessons.try: Clap a 7/8 pattern grouped 2+2+3.

learn: Tempo terms are Italian: largo (very slow), adagio (slow), andante (walking), moderato, allegro (fast), presto (very fast).
Metronome marks show beats per minute: ♩ = 120.
Rubato means flexible tempo for expression.
lessons.try: Play a tune at three tempo markings with a metronome.

learn: Treble lines E-G-B-D-F; spaces F-A-C-E. Bass lines G-B-D-F-A; spaces A-C-E-G.
Middle C connects the two clefs on the grand staff.
Fluent reading comes from daily practice.
lessons.try: Name 20 notes in one minute using flashcards.

learn: Ledger lines extend the staff above or below.
An octave is eight letter names apart; the higher note vibrates twice as fast.
Octave markings (8va) tell you to play an octave higher.
check: An octave is ___ letter names apart.
lessons.try: Write a melody that uses ledger lines.

learn: Sharps raise, flats lower and naturals cancel a sharp or flat.
An accidental lasts until the end of the measure.
Enharmonic notes sound the same but have different names: C♯ and D♭.
check: A natural sign ___ a sharp or flat.
lessons.try: Find five enharmonic pairs on a keyboard.

learn: Sharp keys follow the order F♯, C♯, G♯, D♯, A♯, E♯, B♯.
Flat keys follow B♭, E♭, A♭, D♭, G♭, C♭, F♭.
Each major key shares its signature with a relative minor three half steps below.
check: The relative minor of G major is...
lessons.try: Write key signatures for D major and B♭ major.

learn: An interval is the distance between two notes.
Count letter names inclusively: C to E is a third; C to G is a fifth.
Quality matters: major, minor, perfect, augmented and diminished.
check: C to C an octave higher is a...
lessons.try: Sing intervals from a starting note using familiar songs as references.

learn: Pentatonic scales use five notes and appear in folk music worldwide.
The chromatic scale uses all twelve half steps.
The blues scale adds a "blue note" to the minor pentatonic.
check: The chromatic scale uses all ___ half steps.
The black keys form a ___ scale.
lessons.try: Improvise on the black keys (a pentatonic scale).

learn: In a major key, I, IV and V are major; ii, iii and vi are minor; vii° is diminished.
In C major: C, Dm, Em, F, G, Am, B°.
Lowercase Roman numerals show minor chords.
check: In C major, the IV chord is...
lessons.try: Play all seven triads in C major.

learn: A seventh chord adds a fourth note: G7 = G, B, D, F.
The V7 chord pulls strongly to I.
Inversions put a different note in the bass.
check: Inversions put a different note in the...
lessons.try: Play C major in root position, first inversion and second inversion.

learn: A cadence is a musical punctuation mark.
An authentic cadence (V-I) sounds final; a half cadence (ending on V) sounds unfinished.
A plagal cadence (IV-I) is the "Amen" cadence.
lessons.try: Play each cadence and describe how it feels.

learn: Strophic form repeats the same music for each verse (AAA).
Binary (AB), ternary (ABA), rondo (ABACA), theme and variations.
Twelve-bar blues is a form used in many songs.
lessons.try: Identify the form of three songs.

learn: Monophony is a single melody line; homophony is melody with chords; polyphony is several independent melodies.
Heterophony is variations of the same melody at once.
Texture can change during a piece.
lessons.try: Listen to three pieces and identify their textures.

learn: A canon has voices imitating the same melody, starting at different times.
A fugue develops a short subject through imitation in several voices.
Bach was a master of the fugue.
check: Bach was a master of the...
lessons.try: Sing "Frère Jacques" as a canon.

learn: Dynamics range from ppp to fff.
Phrasing shapes melodies like sentences, with rises and falls.
Breathing at phrase ends helps singers and wind players.
lessons.try: Perform a melody with planned dynamics and phrasing.

learn: Staccato (short), legato (smooth), accent (>), tenuto (held full value), marcato (strongly accented).
A slur connects different notes smoothly; a tie joins the same note.
Articulation changes character dramatically.
lessons.try: Play a scale with four different articulations.

learn: Timbre is tone colour.
Orchestration is choosing which instruments play which parts.
Composers like Ravel were masters of orchestration.
lessons.try: Assign instruments to a melody to create two different moods.

learn: Medieval (500-1400): chant and early polyphony.
Renaissance (1400-1600): rich vocal polyphony, madrigals.
Baroque (1600-1750): Bach, Handel, Vivaldi; opera and the concerto.
lessons.try: Make a timeline with one composer per era.

learn: Classical (1750-1820): Haydn, Mozart, Beethoven; balance and clarity.
Romantic (1820-1900): Chopin, Schumann, Verdi, Tchaikovsky; emotion and drama.
Beethoven bridged the two eras.
lessons.try: Compare a Mozart and a Tchaikovsky piece.

learn: Impressionism: Debussy and Ravel.
Composers experimented with atonality, minimalism and electronics.
Film and game music use orchestral traditions today.
lessons.try: Listen to a minimalist piece and describe its repetition.

learn: Spirituals came from enslaved African Americans.
The blues developed in the Mississippi Delta around 1900.
Scott Joplin was the "King of Ragtime".
check: Scott Joplin was the King of...
lessons.try: Listen to "Maple Leaf Rag" (1899) and describe it.

learn: Jazz developed in New Orleans from blues, ragtime and brass bands.
Louis Armstrong and Duke Ellington were jazz giants.
The swing era (1930s-1940s) featured big bands for dancing.
check: The swing era was in the...
lessons.try: Identify the solos in a jazz recording.

learn: Country grew from Appalachian folk and blues.
Rock and roll (1950s) combined rhythm and blues with country.
Hip-hop began in the Bronx, New York, in the 1970s.
check: Rock and roll combined R&B and...
lessons.try: Make a family tree of American popular music styles.

learn: West African drumming ensembles use polyrhythms and call-and-response.
Griots are storytellers and musicians who keep oral history.
The kora is a 21-string harp-lute.
lessons.try: Perform a polyrhythm with classmates.

learn: Indian classical music uses ragas and talas.
Chinese instruments include the erhu (two-string fiddle) and the pipa (lute).
Arabic music uses maqam scales with notes between Western pitches.
lessons.try: Listen to an erhu solo.

learn: Irish traditional music uses fiddle, tin whistle and bodhrán.
Flamenco from Spain combines song, guitar and dance.
Latin American styles include salsa, tango, samba and cumbia.
check: The tin whistle is used in...
lessons.try: Compare two world styles in a chart.

learn: Strong melodies have a shape, a high point and a balance of steps and leaps.
Repetition makes melodies memorable; variation keeps interest.
End on the tonic to sound finished.
lessons.try: Compose a 16-bar melody in a major key.

learn: Add chords that fit the melody notes.
Choose instruments and textures for each section.
Notation software or the music keyboard can help.
lessons.try: Harmonise your melody with I, IV and V chords.

learn: Prepare with slow practice, then full run-throughs.
Manage nerves with breathing and positive self-talk.
Reflect on performances to improve.
lessons.try: Perform your composition and write a reflection.
